item.title: Middle East conflict causes surge in gas flaring and emissions
item.description: The war in Iran has caused a spike in gas flaring across the Middle East is adding to greenhouse gas emissions as energy infrastructure disruptions linked to regional conflict force producers to burn excess fuel.

item.title: Iran parliament deputy speaker rules out any negotiations with US
item.description: Iran's parliament deputy speaker says there will be no negotiations with the US, the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen, and Tehran will push the conflict into the energy and economic sphere.

item.title: Saudi Arabia's Neom cancels major Trojena ski village contract
item.description: Neom terminates Eversendai's structural steel contract at Trojena ski village, citing the geopolitical situation, in the second giga-project cancellation this month as regional conflict adds to spending pressure.

item.title: Tel Aviv stocks plummet despite brief recovery after US halt on Iran strikes
item.description: Israeli stocks on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange deepened their losses on March 24, hitting a new intraday low at approximately 16:53 local time. The TA-35 index fell approximately 2%, whilst the TA-90 index declined 1.8%.

item.title: Which countries in Europe and Asia have the most reserve coal-fired generating capacity in reserve?
item.description: Natural gas prices have already doubled since the start of the war in the Middle East and are expected to rise higher as the last of Qatar’s LNG exports arrive at their destinations. Now everyone is switching to coal.

item.title: Pakistan offers Islamabad as venue for US-Iran peace talks
item.description: Pakistan offers Islamabad as a venue for US-Iran peace talks as Prime Minister Sharif confirms back-channel diplomacy with both Washington and Tehran, with a US delegation expected within days.

item.title: IMF: America's perilous fiscal path
item.description: In 1990, US public debt stood at 43% of gross national product (GNP) and former President Bush thought that was too much. Today the debt is 124% of GDP and still going up. That leaves the US in a perilous position.

item.title: Israel welcomes Lebanon move to expel Iranian envoy
item.description: Israel’s foreign minister Gideon Sa’ar has welcomed Lebanon’s reported decision to expel Iran’s ambassador-designate, urging Beirut to take further steps to curb the influence of Hezbollah amid heightened regional tensions.

item.title: UAE restarts key gas plant as Hormuz disruption curbs LNG exports
item.description: The United Arab Emirates has resumed operations at its largest gas processing facility following an attack that halted output, even as exports of liquefied natural gas remain severely constrained by disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Number of ships passing through Hormuz rising after toll system established
item.description: The number of ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz is increasing as after a $2mn fee was established and the inform permits-for-passage system is smoothed by use.
